ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Urban Ecology
Description: Urban Ecology is an interdisciplinary field concerned with the interrelationships among social, environmental, and economic systems, with the goal of enhancing the vitality and sustainability of places and communities. The University of Utah's Urban Ecology program is designed to respond to problems and opportunities that exist in cities, suburbs, small towns, and rural places for example, environmental management, fragile landscape protection, disaster resilience, Recreation and Tourism, Public Lands Planning, Rapid Population Growth, Regional Transportation, Energy Production, and Sprawl. The urban ecology program in City and Metropolitan Planning at the University of Utah takes an action-oriented, community-engaged approach to help students gain the knowledge and skills to foster sustainable, resilient, and equitable communities. As a student of the Urban Ecology program, you will take classes in urban ecology, planning, field studies, economics, law and social justice; you can also choose from a variety of electives topics, such as green infrastructure, sustainable development, community leadership and cities in literature. In your senior year, you will do an internship and take on a real world problem in the Ecological Planning Workshop. The undergraduate program in Urban Ecology will prepare students for professional careers in environmental and sustainability planning, public health, public policy, and community development and planning.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Writing and Rhetoric Studies
Bachelor of Science in Writing and Rhetoric Studies
Description: Rhetoric is the study of effective Speaking & writing: it is the art of argument & persuasion. Through the Writing & Rhetoric Studies program, you will become a strong analytical thinker & proficient writer. Students of this program learn rhetorical analysis & the ways that culture & society shape what we define as “literacy,” giving you critical thinking skills & social awareness that can be applied to a number of pursuits. Students in the program choose courses from topics such as everyday rhetorics, digital storytelling, writing popular non-fiction, professional discourse, grammar & stylistics, writing as a social practice, & others. The culminating experience of the program is a senior seminar, synthesizing all of the student's undergraduate work into a portfolio piece. Employers consistently rank written communication skills as among the most-desired abilities in job candidates, & strong writing & argumentation abilities are excellent assets for graduate-level coursework.
